observation.visible_scene: An elevated, oblique view of a sandy shoreline. Foaming surf occupies the upper-left band, a wide diagonal stretch of wet/dry sand fills the center, and a wedge of green vegetation sits in the lower-right corner. A dark upright object (driftwood or rock) stands on the sand toward the right, and a rocky outcrop/cliff edge appears at the far right in later frames.
visible_changes: The breaking surf continuously changes shape: the white foam edge advances and retreats across the sand and the bubble texture churns frame-to-frame (an already ongoing wave process, not a single onset).

The viewpoint slowly pans/tracks to the right (and slightly downward): early frames show only open sand and foam, while later frames bring a dark upright driftwood/rock piece into view on the right side of the beach and then a larger rocky outcrop at the extreme right edge.

The green vegetation wedge in the lower-right corner grows progressively larger in the frame as the camera moves, while the diagonal shoreline shifts its apparent position relative to the frame edges.
The dark rock/driftwood and the rocky outcrop remain fixed on the ground; their changing position across the frame is due to camera movement, not their own motion.
The relative ordering of static features (foam band above sand, vegetation below-right, rock to the right of the open sand) is preserved throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rightward pan continues beyond the last frame or reverses.
The origin of the incoming wave set and the full extent of the beach/cliff outside the cropped view.
Whether the dark upright object is wood or stone (texture is too low-resolution to confirm).
uncertain_details: Exact camera mechanism (pure pan vs. lateral translation along the coast) cannot be distinguished from the background alone.
Minor apparent shifts of the shoreline diagonal could be camera motion rather than wave wash.
The identity of the green area (cliff-top slope vs. dune vegetation) is not certain.
